1.note: The expression **thus says** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **creator**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is the one who created you]

1.q: בֹּרַאֲ⁠ךָ֣ & תִּירָא֙ & גְאַלְתִּ֔י⁠ךָ קָרָ֥אתִי בְ⁠שִׁמְ⁠ךָ֖ & אָֽתָּה
1.note: In verses 1–5 and 22–26, the terms “you” and “your” are singular because they are addressed to the Israelites personified as their ancestor Jacob or Israel. So use singular forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fashioner**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the one who formed you]
The word **for** introduces the reason the people do not need to fear: Yahweh has redeemed them. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason.

Here, **your name** represents your identity as a person who belongs to Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I call you as one who belongs to me]

2.q: כִּֽי־תַעֲבֹ֤ר בַּ⁠מַּ֨יִם֙ אִתְּ⁠ךָ־אָ֔נִי וּ⁠בַ⁠נְּהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּ⁠ךָ כִּֽי־תֵלֵ֤ךְ בְּמוֹ־אֵשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶ֔ה וְ⁠לֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר־בָּֽ⁠ךְ
2.note: The word that the ULT translates as **When** indicates that Yahweh will be present with the people at the same time as when they pass through dangerous experiences. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could describe the time relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [While you pass through the waters, I {will be} with you, and through the rivers, they will not overwhelm you. While you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and the flame will not burn you up]

2.q: כִּֽי תַעֲבֹ֤ר בַּ⁠מַּ֨יִם֙ אִתְּ⁠ךָ אָ֔נִי וּ⁠בַ⁠נְּהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּ⁠ךָ
2.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if dangerous and overwhelming experiences were **waters** and **rivers** in which a person could be swept away. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [When you face overwhelming dangers, I will be with you, and they will not overcome you]

2.q: כִּֽי תֵלֵ֤ךְ בְּמוֹ אֵשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶ֔ה וְ⁠לֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽ⁠ךְ
2.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if dangerous and painful experiences were a **fire** and a **flame** that could burn a person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [When you experience dangerous situations, you will not be harmed, and they will not destroy you]

The expression **be burned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the fire will not burn you]

3.note: The word **For** introduces the reason the people do not need to be afraid: Yahweh is their God and Savior. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason. See the UST.

3.q: נָתַ֤תִּי כָפְרְ⁠ךָ֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם כּ֥וּשׁ וּ⁠סְבָ֖א תַּחְתֶּֽי⁠ךָ
3.note: The names **Egypt**, **Cush**, and **Seba** represent the peoples of those nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I give the people of Egypt {as} your ransom, the people of Cush and Seba in place of you]
The word **Seba** is the name of a place.

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I give Cush and Seba in place of you]

4.note: The word **Because** introduces the reason Yahweh will give other peoples in place of his people: they are precious and honored and loved by him. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason. Alternate translation: [Since]

Yahweh is using **you are precious in my eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you are valuable to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you are valuable to me]

The expression **are honored** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I have honored you]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I love** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize his personal love for Israel. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [and I myself love you]
Here, **your soul** represents you yourself as a living person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your life]

5.note: The word **for** introduces the reason the people do not need to be afraid: Yahweh is with them. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason. Alternate translation: [because]

Yahweh is referring to all directions by naming two of them, **the rising** of the sun in the east and **the setting** in the west. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the east I will bring your descendants, and from the west I will gather you]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people’s descendants were their **seed**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your offspring]

6.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [I will say to the north to give and to the south not to keep back.]

Yahweh is speaking of **the north** and **the south** as if they were living things that could hear and obey his commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will command the people in the north to release my people, and the people in the south to not keep them back.]

Yahweh is referring to all directions by naming two of them, **the north** and **the south**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I will say to every direction, ‘Give,’ and ‘May you not keep back]

6.q: הָבִ֤יאִי בָנַ⁠י֙ מֵ⁠רָח֔וֹק וּ⁠בְנוֹתַ֖⁠י מִ⁠קְצֵ֥ה הָ⁠אָֽרֶץ
6.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the Israelites were his **sons** and his **daughters**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Bring back from faraway those people who are like sons and daughters to me]

The imperative **Bring** is feminine in Hebrew because it is addressed to **the south**. However, here the south and the north (also feminine) represent all directions. Use the appropriate grammatical gender in your language.

7.note: The expression **called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [whom I have called by my name]

The phrase **called by my name** represents belonging to Yahweh as his own people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the ones who belong to me]

8.q: עַם עִוֵּ֖ר וְ⁠עֵינַ֣יִם יֵ֑שׁ וְ⁠חֵרְשִׁ֖ים וְ⁠אָזְנַ֥יִם לָֽ⁠מוֹ
8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people who cannot perceive spiritual truth were physically **blind** and **deaf**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a people who cannot perceive spiritual truth, even though they have eyes, and those who cannot understand it, even though they have ears]

By **yet there are eyes** and **yet ears {are} to them**, Yahweh means that the people ought to be able to see and hear. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [though they ought to be able to see … though they ought to be able to hear]
The pronoun **them** refers to the people who are blind and deaf. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [are to those people]

9.note: The expression **gathered together** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [have come together]

The expression **assembled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the peoples have come together]

These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [All of the nations are gathered together; indeed, the peoples are assembled]

9.q: מִ֤י בָ⁠הֶם֙ יַגִּ֣יד זֹ֔את וְ⁠רִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת יַשְׁמִיעֻ֑⁠נוּ
9.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that none of the nations’ gods declared these events beforehand. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [None of them declared this, and they did not make predictions that were true]
The pronoun **them** refers to the nations and the peoples. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Who among these nations and peoples]
The pronoun **they** refers to the nations. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the nations made us hear]
Here, **that** marks **they may be righteous** as the goal or purpose of bringing their witnesses. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.
If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [that they may say that it is true]

10.note: In verses 10-15 and 18–19, the words “you” and “your” are plural because they refer to the Israelites as Yahweh’s **witnesses**. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **the declaration of Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, declare]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **declaration**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh declared]

Here, **so that** marks **you may know and believe in me** as the goal or purpose of Yahweh making the people his witnesses and chosen servant. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [in order that you may know and believe in me]
Yahweh is using the expression **To my face** to mean “before” or “previous to.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Before me]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and after me, no god will be formed]

The expression **was formed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one formed any god]

11.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately and repeating it, even though the verb translated as **am** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he alone is Yahweh and there is no other savior. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit or repeated pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the emphasis here. Alternate translation: [I myself am Yahweh]

Yahweh told them that **there is no savior except me**. If it would appear in your language that Yahweh was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [and I alone am the savior]

12.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I declared** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who declared these things. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I myself declared]

The word **you** is plural here because it refers to the people of Israel. If your language distinguishes between singular and plural forms of you, use the plural form here. Alternate translation: [And all of you are my witnesses]
See how you translated the similar expression in 43:10.

13.note: Here, **my hand** represents Yahweh’s power and control. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from my power and control]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that no one can reverse what he does. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I act, and no one can turn it back.] or [I act, and no one can oppose what I do]

14.q: כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְ⁠כֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
14.note: The expression **Thus says** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **Redeemer**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the one who saves you]

The phrase **For your sake** introduces the reason Yahweh will act against Babylon, namely, to benefit his people. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason. Alternate translation: [For your good] or [Because of you]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I will bring the Chaldeans down in the ships of their rejoicing]

15.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **Creator**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the one who created Israel]

16.q: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַ⁠נּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּ⁠יָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ
16.note: The expression **Thus says** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

16.q: הַ⁠נּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּ⁠יָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ וּ⁠בְ⁠מַ֥יִם עַזִּ֖ים נְתִיבָֽה
16.note: The implication is that this refers to the time when Yahweh divided the sea so that the Israelites could escape from Egypt. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the one having made a way in the sea and a path in the mighty waters so that the Israelites could escape from Egypt]

17.note: Yahweh is using the terms **chariot and horse** and **army** to represent the entire Egyptian army. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the entire Egyptian army]

Yahweh is using the adjective **mighty** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and mighty soldiers]

The pronoun **they** refers to the Egyptian army with its chariots and horses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [together the Egyptian army lay down and did not arise]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a wick** stops burning when it is snuffed out, so **they**, the Egyptian army, were completely destroyed. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [they were quenched like a wick that is snuffed out and can no longer burn]

18.note: Yahweh is using the adjective **former** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [things that happened before]

Yahweh is using the adjective **ancient** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and may you not regard things of old]

19.q: הִנְ⁠נִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ עַתָּ֣ה תִצְמָ֔ח הֲ⁠ל֖וֹא תֵֽדָע֑וּ⁠הָ אַ֣ף אָשִׂ֤ים בַּ⁠מִּדְבָּר֙ דֶּ֔רֶךְ בִּֽ⁠ישִׁמ֖וֹן נְהָרֽוֹת
19.note: Yahweh will make a way in the wilderness as the next stage of the new thing that he is now beginning to do. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [Behold me, doing the new. Now it sprouts; do you not know it? Then I will make a way in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland]

Yahweh is using **Behold me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Look at what I am about to do.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Watch what I will do]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the new thing he is doing were a plant that **sprouts** from the ground. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now it is already happening]

Yahweh is using the question form to urge the people to recognize the new thing he is doing. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [you should know it.]

20.q: תְּכַבְּדֵ֨⁠נִי֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֔ה תַּנִּ֖ים וּ⁠בְנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה
20.note: Yahweh is speaking of **the beasts of the field** as if they were able to **honor** him as people do. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Even the wild animals, jackals and ostriches, will appreciate the benefit of what I do]

Yahweh is using **the daughters of the ostrich** as a common expression of the culture to mean “ostriches.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the ostriches]

The word **because** introduces the reason the wild animals will honor Yahweh: he will provide water for them in the wilderness. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason. Alternate translation: [since]

Here, **for** marks **my people, my chosen, to drink** as the goal or purpose of Yahweh giving waters in the wilderness. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [I will give rivers in the wasteland so that my people, my chosen, will have water to drink]

Yahweh is using the adjective **chosen** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [my chosen ones]

21.q: עַם זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔⁠י תְּהִלָּתִ֖⁠י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ
21.note: The second statement, **they will recount my praise**, expresses the goal or purpose for which Yahweh **formed this people**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [I formed this people for myself so that they will recount my praise]

22.note: Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between all that he has done for his people and their failure to call on him. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yet you have not called on me]
The word **for** introduces the reason the people have not called on Yahweh: they have become weary of him. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason. Alternate translation: [because]

23.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **burnt offerings**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what you burn as offerings]

24.note: Here, **calamus** is a kind of fragrant reed that people used to make perfume and incense. If your readers would not be familiar with what calamus is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [sweet-smelling reeds]

Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what the people failed to give him and what they have actually burdened him with. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Instead,]

**But you have made me serve with your sins; you have wearied me with your iniquities**. These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [you have burdened me with your sins; indeed, you have wearied me with your iniquities]

God is using **you have made me serve** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you have burdened me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you have given me grief with your sins] or [you have burdened me with your sins]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **sins**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with the wrong things you have done]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquities**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with the evil things you have done]

25.q: מֹחֶ֥ה פְשָׁעֶ֖י⁠ךָ לְמַעֲנִ֑⁠י וְ⁠חַטֹּאתֶ֖י⁠ךָ לֹ֥א אֶזְכֹּֽר
25.note: The phrase **for my own sake** introduces the reason Yahweh wipes away the people’s transgressions, namely, for the sake of his own honor. Use a natural way in your language to introduce a reason. Alternate translation: [to benefit me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **transgressions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [your rebellious acts]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **sins**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and I will not remember the wrong things you have done]

26.note: The expression **be judged** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [let us judge this matter together]

Here, the word **that** marks **you may be righteous** as the goal or purpose of the command to **recount**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [to prove that you are righteous]

27.note: The implication is that **Your first father** refers to the earliest ancestor of the people of Israel. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Your earliest ancestor]

28.note: The word translated as **So** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Therefore, I profaned]

Here, **the princes of the sanctuary** represents the priests and leaders who served in the temple. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the priests and leaders of the temple]

The names **Jacob** and **Israel** represent the people who were descended from Jacob, who was also called Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I gave the descendants of Jacob to devotion and the descendants of Israel to revilings]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **devotion**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be given over to destruction]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I gave Israel to revilings]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **revilings**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be mocked]
